ai.subject: Biochemistry & genetics
ai.summary: Reduced glutathione (GSH) is the main intracellular antioxidant that detoxifies reactive oxygen species and maintains protein thiol status. Low GSH leads to oxidative stress, cell injury and contributes to many diseases.

sections.p: GSH is a tripeptide (γ‑glutamyl‑cysteinyl‑glycine) present at millimolar concentrations in most cells. It cycles between reduced (GSH) and oxidized (GSSG) forms, protecting membranes, DNA and enzymes from oxidative damage.
b: Key antioxidant; co‑factor for glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and glutathione S‑transferase (GST)

sections.p: GPx uses GSH to reduce hydrogen peroxide and lipid peroxides, forming GSSG. Glutathione reductase (GR) then uses NADPH to regenerate GSH from GSSG, completing the cycle.
b: GSH + H2O2 → GSSG + 2 H2O (catalyzed by GPx)
GSSG + NADPH + H+ → 2 GSH + NADP+ (catalyzed by GR)

t.b: Is oxidative stress present? Low ratio indicates depleted antioxidant capacity.
Is cellular antioxidant reserve adequate? Low level suggests hemolysis risk or chronic disease.

sections.p: Synthesis is controlled by γ‑glutamylcysteine synthetase (rate‑limiting) and availability of cysteine. NADPH from the pentose‑phosphate pathway fuels GR. Hormones (insulin) and oxidative stress up‑regulate synthesis.
Depletion occurs when production cannot keep up with consumption, as in chronic infections, malnutrition, drug toxicity, or inherited enzyme defects (e.g., G6PD deficiency).
b: Low GSH → unchecked ROS → lipid peroxidation, protein dysfunction, DNA damage
G6PD deficiency limits NADPH → impaired GR activity

sections.p: Reduced GSH is a marker and mediator of disease severity in sepsis, HIV, TB, malaria, hepatitis B, sickle cell disease, and exposure to herbal toxins. Severe depletion can precipitate acute kidney injury, hepatic failure, or hemolysis.
b: Low GSH predicts poorer outcomes in sepsis and malaria
GSH depletion contributes to drug‑induced liver injury

t.a: Serum GSH level in septic patient
t.b: Does oxidative stress correlate with organ failure? Very low GSH (<2 µmol/L) signals high mortality risk.
Is lipid peroxidation increased? Elevated values support oxidative stress when GSH is low.

sections.p: Focus on the GSH‑GPx‑GR cycle, causes of depletion, and clinical scenarios where oxidative stress drives pathology.
b: Remember the equation: 2 GSH + H2O2 → GSSG + 2 H2O
NADPH from PPP is essential for regeneration
Low GSH in malaria, HIV, TB, sickle cell

whenToSeekHelp: Rapidly falling GSH with acute hemolysis, severe sepsis, or acute liver failure requiring intensive care

faq.q: Why is GSH important for red blood cells?
faq.a: RBCs lack nuclei and rely on GSH to neutralize peroxide; depletion leads to membrane damage and hemolysis.
Foods rich in cysteine (e.g., whey, legumes) support synthesis, but severe depletion often needs medical intervention.

faq.q: Is measuring GSH useful in routine labs?
faq.a: It is mainly a research/tertiary‑care test; clinicians infer oxidative stress from surrogate markers when unavailable.

exam: Explain the GSH‑GPx‑GR cycle and write the balanced reaction for hydrogen peroxide reduction.
List three common conditions in low‑resource settings that cause GSH depletion and the clinical consequences.
Interpret a low serum GSH/GSSG ratio in a patient with severe malaria.
